title: Setting: The Candidate Octic and the Galois-Conjugate Product
content: The header fixes the candidate minimal polynomial p(X) = X⁸ − 40X⁶ + 352X⁴ − 960X² + 576 and explains where it comes from: it is the product over the eight sign-conjugates ∏_{ε∈{±1}³}(X − ε₁√2 − ε₂√3 − ε₃√5). Because the conjugate set is closed under flipping all signs, the roots come in ± pairs, forcing p(X)=p(−X) and hence only even powers of X. The coefficients (−40, 352, −960, 576) are the elementary symmetric functions of the eight roots, equivalently obtained from the power sums via Newton's identities. The header is deliberately explicit about scope: it lists what is unconditionally verified (the root family, monicity, degree, integrality, divisibility) and what is left conditional (irreducibility, equivalent to the degree-8 field fact).
mathContext: For distinct primes the field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2,\sqrt3,\sqrt5)$ is multiquadratic of degree $2^3=8$ with Galois group $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^3$ acting by independent sign flips; $\sqrt2+\sqrt3+\sqrt5$ is a primitive element, so $\deg\,\mathrm{minpoly}_{\mathbb{Q}}=8$.

title: The Sign-Independent Isolate-and-Square Computation
content: `conjugates_are_roots` is the heart of the file. It takes arbitrary reals a, b, c with a²=2, b²=3, c²=5 and proves p(a+b+c)=0. The chain: set t=bc (so t²=15 by `mul_pow`); prove the isolating identity (a+b+c)²−6−2t = 2a(a+b+c) by `linear_combination -ha + hb + hc`; square it to get ((a+b+c)²−6−2t)² = 8(a+b+c)² (the √2 is now squared away); finally a single `linear_combination` with explicit polynomial multipliers of this relation and of t²=15 collapses the degree-8 goal to 0. The decisive point is that NO step references the signs of a, b, c — only their squares — so the very same proof certifies every one of the eight conjugates ε₁√2+ε₂√3+ε₃√5 (take a∈{±√2}, etc.). This is the computational realization of the Galois-conjugate product.

title: Specializing to α = √2 + √3 + √5
content: `aeval_minpoly_candidate` transports the real-number identity into the polynomial-algebra setting. It introduces (√2)²=2, (√3)²=3, (√5)²=5 via `Real.sq_sqrt`, unfolds `Polynomial.aeval` of the candidate octic with a targeted `simp only` (`map_sub`, `map_add`, `map_mul`, `map_pow`, `map_ofNat`, `aeval_X`), and then closes by applying `conjugates_are_roots` to the principal square roots. The polynomial's rational coefficients pass through the ℚ→ℝ algebra map cleanly, so no `push_cast` is needed.
mathContext: $\mathrm{aeval}_{\sqrt2+\sqrt3+\sqrt5}(X^8-40X^6+352X^4-960X^2+576)=0$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ — the principal conjugate is a root.

title: Monicity, Degree 8, and Integrality
content: Three short structural facts. `cand_monic` proves the octic is monic with the `monicity!` tactic; `cand_natDegree` proves it has degree 8 with `compute_degree!` — both automate what in the sister n=2 entry required an explicit `natDegree` computation. `sqrt_sum_isIntegral` then packages the monic polynomial with the root witness into Mathlib's `IsIntegral` anonymous constructor ⟨p, cand_monic, aeval_minpoly_candidate⟩, certifying that √2+√3+√5 is integral (algebraic) over ℚ.
mathContext: A monic polynomial of degree 8 with $\alpha$ as a root shows $\alpha$ is integral over $\mathbb{Q}$ of degree at most 8.

title: Divisibility and the Conditional Minimal-Polynomial Identity
content: `minpoly_dvd_cand` records the unconditional fact minpoly ℚ (√2+√3+√5) ∣ p, via `minpoly.dvd` applied to the root witness — the minimal polynomial always divides any annihilator. `minpoly_eq_of_irreducible` then states the headline identity minpoly ℚ α = p, but with irreducibility of p over ℚ as an EXPLICIT HYPOTHESIS, discharged through `minpoly.eq_of_irreducible_of_monic`. This is an honest formulation: irreducibility is equivalent to [ℚ(√2+√3+√5):ℚ]=8, the multiquadratic field-degree fact recorded as the parent entry's oq-04. Mathlib v4.26.0 lacks the multi-quadratic API needed to prove it, and — unlike the n=2 quartic, whose irreducibility is a finite coefficient analysis — the degree-8 brute force does not scale, so the assumption is hypothesized rather than asserted as an axiom (keeping the file genuinely axiom-free).
mathContext: $\mathrm{minpoly}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)\mid p$ always; and $\mathrm{minpoly}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)=p$ iff $p$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ iff $[\mathbb{Q}(\alpha):\mathbb{Q}]=8$.
